Both are presidential memoranda to the Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board addressing international air-carrier recommendations, distinguishing approved denials from recommendations withheld or disapproved, and grounding the decision in foreign-policy and national-interest considerations. They also share a progression from review of the Board's recommendation, through acknowledgment of the Board's objectives or evidence, to rejection because the record does not justify the competitive consequences. C19 and C05 are related CAB precedents, but their shared language and operative structure are less extensive.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"After considerable deliberation I have concluded that the recommendations of the Civil Aeronautics Board ... should, with minor exceptions set forth at the end of this memorandum, be disapproved.","parent_excerpt":"I have carefully considered the recommendation of the Civil Aeronautics Board ... and have decided (a) to approve the Board's denial of applications and (b) to withhold my approval in other respects.","explanation":"Both memoranda divide a CAB disposition into a generally rejected portion and specifically approved exceptions."},{"child_excerpt":"My decision not to approve the Board's principal recommendations is predicated solely on considerations of foreign policy, a responsibility that is mine and which the Board, of course, does not share.","parent_excerpt":"I have reviewed the case on the basis of foreign policy and defense considerations together with other elements of the national interest that are within my particular responsibilities","explanation":"Distinctively parallel language invokes the President's special responsibility for foreign-policy and national-interest review of CAB recommendations."},{"child_excerpt":"The study made by the Board is excellent. Much evidence is set forth in support of the Board's recommendations ... My review of the record ... persuades me that our foreign relations would be adversely affected","parent_excerpt":"I appreciate the Board's objectives ... This concern is not met by the record now before me.","explanation":"Each acknowledges the Board's work or objectives before concluding that the record does not overcome concerns about expanded international air-carrier competition."}]}
